title: Power Stack Watchlist
method: Action-oriented queue combining business quality, plausible upside, downside/funding risk, valuation, technical location, current theme significance and usefulness beside the existing portfolio. Diversification cannot rescue a mediocre stock; portfolio fit only helps rank already-good ideas. Social/creator/TradingView prominence is discovery-only until independently verified.
marketRegime: The immediate market gate is higher long-end yields plus renewed energy/product inflation. Physical AI infrastructure remains structurally strong, agriculture/fertilizer and energy-security rerouting are phasing in, and software is showing selective relative strength. Prefer current cash flow and differentiated return drivers; demand better prices for crowded duration.

buckets.label: Buy / Accumulate
buckets.description: Price, business quality and current theme setup are aligned enough for staged entry.

buckets.label: Selective / Retest
buckets.description: Good business/theme, but current price or portfolio overlap requires a better level or confirmation.

buckets.label: Wait / Confirm
buckets.description: Interesting exposure, but current risk/reward or cyclical timing is not strong enough to force.

buckets.label: Avoid / High Risk
buckets.description: Theme may be attractive, but financing, valuation, dilution or execution risk currently dominates.

candidates.name: CF Industries
candidates.entry: $123–127 preferred; small starter only if ~$128–130 holds
candidates.invalidation: Sustained <$118 or a sharp collapse in nitrogen margins / US gas advantage
candidates.thesis: Best current commodity-agriculture expression. Nitrogen is harder to defer than most farm inputs, North American gas economics remain advantaged, and current cash flow/buybacks reduce reliance on multiple expansion. Adds a genuinely different earnings driver beside the existing energy/power holdings.

candidates.name: Corteva
candidates.invalidation: Sustained <$78 or weakening seed pricing / separation economics
candidates.thesis: Highest-quality agriculture compounder in the current queue. Farmers can trim some inputs but still need to plant; genetics and yield resilience gain value as weather/input volatility rises. Strong portfolio diversification with less commodity beta than CF.

candidates.name: Bunge Global
candidates.invalidation: Sustained <$106 or Viterra integration / crush-margin deterioration
candidates.thesis: Diversified exposure to crop-flow volatility, crushing/refining and global food logistics rather than a single crop. Food/feed volumes are resilient while margins remain cyclical. One of the best portfolio-complement ideas because the return driver differs from oil and AI-power.

candidates.name: Cameco
candidates.invalidation: Sustained <$92 or deterioration in contracting / mine / Westinghouse evidence
candidates.thesis: Prefer operating uranium/fuel scarcity and Westinghouse exposure over pre-revenue reactor hype. Nuclear is no longer the freshest market story, but the business setup and current support zone remain attractive.

candidates.name: Cheniere Energy
candidates.invalidation: Sustained <$268 or rapid normalization of global LNG scarcity/spreads
candidates.theme: LNG · energy security · Europe / Asia rerouting
candidates.thesis: Energy-security rerouting has moved sharply higher in theme significance. US LNG infrastructure is a cleaner toll-road than chasing spot gas, but the stock has already run toward resistance and overlaps the portfolio's broader energy exposure.

candidates.name: Quanta Services
candidates.invalidation: Sustained break below ~$560 with backlog/order deterioration
candidates.thesis: Record backlog/RPO and FCF keep PWR among the highest-quality AI-power bottlenecks. It ranks below the new agriculture ideas only because long yields raise the valuation hurdle and the existing portfolio already owns meaningful power/data-centre exposure.

candidates.name: Eaton
candidates.thesis: Electrical orders and backlog remain extraordinary, but the current bond regime is a genuine multiple headwind. Excellent company; buy the physical bottleneck at a sensible price rather than paying any price for the theme.

candidates.name: Nutrien
candidates.invalidation: Sustained <$69 or clear fertilizer demand destruction / potash deterioration
candidates.thesis: Diversifies across potash, nitrogen and retail. Potash is more deferrable than nitrogen, so NTR ranks below CF, but it remains a solid cash-generative hedge against prolonged fertilizer scarcity.

candidates.name: SLB
candidates.invalidation: Sustained <$52 or Kelvion integration / leverage economics deteriorate
candidates.thesis: The $4.1bn Kelvion acquisition makes SLB a measurable oil-services + AI-cooling crossover. Management targets $4.5–5.0bn of data-centre revenue and $700–800m EBITDA by 2028. Fresh and differentiated, but acquisition/integration risk prevents a higher rank.

candidates.name: Valmont Industries
candidates.thesis: Useful crossover between grid infrastructure and a possible irrigation-cycle bottom. Agriculture capex is deferrable, so this is a second-stage weather/farm-income trade with the grid segment providing ballast.

candidates.name: Salesforce
candidates.invalidation: Sustained <$225 or AI monetisation/cRPO/FCF momentum fades
candidates.thesis: Strong Q2 evidence makes CRM the best current proof that incumbent software can monetise AI: revenue and cRPO grew while Agentforce/Data 360 and FCF accelerated. The stock already jumped more than 20% after earnings, so the thesis is attractive but the chase is not.

candidates.name: CrowdStrike
candidates.thesis: Mission-critical security plus strong ARR makes CRWD a real software winner, but it closed essentially at its 52-week high after a large earnings gap and carries an extreme valuation. Do not confuse quality with an attractive entry.

candidates.name: Freeport-McMoRan
candidates.invalidation: Sustained <$64 or structural copper-demand/supply thesis break
candidates.thesis: Copper remains structurally important, but current pricing still contains tariff/inventory distortions and FCX is close to the recent $80.24 high. Structural yes; chase no.

candidates.name: Symbotic
candidates.invalidation: Sustained <$35 or deployment/revenue/EBITDA momentum rolls over
candidates.thesis: Commercial automation remains the most underwritable robotics wave and Symbotic has current revenue/profit evidence. It is not a top macro theme today, so this is a company-specific support setup rather than a momentum chase.

candidates.name: AGCO Corporation
candidates.entry: No aggressive entry until crop/farm margins improve
candidates.confirmation: Evidence of farm-income recovery + improving equipment orders
candidates.invalidation: Further equipment-demand cuts or persistent fertilizer/fuel squeeze
candidates.thesis: Potential 2027 operating leverage if crop prices restore farm income after deferred equipment purchases. Food is a staple; machinery is not. Wait for the farm-economics turn.

candidates.name: NuScale Power
candidates.entry: No entry until commercial/financing evidence improves
candidates.thesis: Nuclear remains strategically strong, but higher yields make venture-style reactor equities less attractive. Operating fuel/components and cash-generating infrastructure remain the preferred expressions.
